rationale_evidence.anchor: Epistemic status should depend on evidence/criteria, not emotional or outcome preference. ... Truth evaluation \perp outcome preference
rationale_evidence.statement: From Chapter 12's equanimity verses (fixed and free from disturbance amid happiness/distress, honor/dishonor, friend/enemy, praise/criticism): Evaluation != Reaction -- a Kernel should not change a proposition's epistemic status merely because it is praised, attacked, desirable or undesirable. Proposed invariant: epistemic status should depend on evidence/criteria, not emotional or outcome preference; formalized as Truth evaluation _|_ (independent of) outcome preference, warning against a weak-system failure mode where a desired outcome C causes evidence A to be reinterpreted as supporting C. Also proposes a Perturbation Resistance property: given external disturbance epsilon on K_t, a robust Kernel should route through Buddhi to evaluate epsilon rather than blindly computing K_{t+1}=f(K_t,epsilon).
